elements.element: Customer has a right to terminate for convenience (Agreement and/or Order Form)
elements.evidence: "Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience"
"upon 30 days' prior written notice to Vendor"

elements.element: Pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on such termination
elements.evidence: "Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination"

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term
elements.evidence: "Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a committed term."
Inserted clause uses "30 days' prior written notice", shorter than the 60–90 day fallback window

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is stated; instead "Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees"

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at end of a term on 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "Vendor has no right to terminate ... for convenience during a committed term" — no end-of-term 90-day Vendor right granted

reasons: All four preferred atomic elements are satisfied by the inserted Section 9.4: Customer convenience right, 30 days' written notice, refund of prepaid Fees for the post-termination period (pro-rata), and an express bar on Vendor convenience termination during a committed term.
Fallback is not met (and need not be, since the locked target is preferred): notice is 30 rather than 60–90 days, no early-termination fee mechanic, and no end-of-term Vendor convenience right.

Minimality is satisfied: a single concise insertion filling a genuine gap in Section 9, no rewrite of Sections 9.1–9.5, no imported fallback terms in the operative text (the fee cap appears only in the non-operative comment).

Intent concern: Section 2.1 states the three-year take-or-pay commitment is "without reduction or termination rights," which directly contradicts the new 9.4 convenience right and leaves an unresolved conflict as to whether the committed spend survives termination. Add "Notwithstanding Section 2.1," (or a conforming carve-out in 2.1) and state the effect on the remaining committed spend to remove the contradiction.
